title: Grateful Dead Live at Olympia Theater on 1972-05-03

ai_review.summary: Near‑perfect soundboard capture of a high‑energy Paris show with smoking The Other One, China > Rider and standout Hurts Me Too slide‑guitar.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised as one of the tour’s highlights – tight set transitions, soaring vocals and monster jams (especially The Other One and the China > Rider suite) make it a fan favorite.  The soundboard source is remarkably clean, with crystal‑clear separation, only a tiny dropout on the final Other One reprise that most listeners barely notice.  Overall the recording delivers both musical brilliance and technical fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 70 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 ★, citing exceptional performance and a clean soundboard source; only minor technical glitches are noted, yielding an overall rating near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean, crisp SBD with excellent channel separation and minimal digital noise; a very small dropout on the final Other One reprise and occasional tiny zap, but overall near‑perfect clarity.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Seamless transitions – especially the China > Rider segue and the Truckin' > Space > Too > Drums jam – keep the momentum high throughout both sets.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is highlighted on Hurts Me Too, Sing Me Back Home and The Other One; reviewers rave about his tone, soaring solos and vocal delivery.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass is described as ‘bombs’ and ‘maniacal’, driving the extended jams in The Other One and providing a powerful backbone throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir contributes strong chord work and melodic interplay, especially noted during the jam sections of The Other One and the closing sequences.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s organ adds lush texture (e.g., on Sing Me Back Home) and his solo on Jack Straw receives specific praise; overall keyboard work is praised for its warmth and depth.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann delivers tight, jazzy drum breaks and snappy fills that elevate the jam sections, particularly before the Other One reprise.
